main_body: Hip roof of green tiles over a white plaster wall with red pillars and a dark lattice double door, on a grey stone base
top_band: At x=48/71: gold ridge finials at rows 0-3, then a light green ridge cap at rows 4-8, then the tiled roof slope at rows 10-41 in a gradient of greens, which reads as a large sloped top surface
evidence: The roof is a large foreshortened sloped surface with a ridge cap and flared eaves, as in the Beodeul house references. Rows 42-43 are a lit eave edge. Rows 28-41 are darker, giving shadow near the eave. Below it sit the red lintel beam and the wall face (rows 44-73). The lattice door is inset with dark tones, and the pillars are tinted separately. The roof slope and the front wall are both clearly drawn, so the contract is satisfied.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5-6 green steps with per-tile highlights, which is good. But the dark edge pixels are 83% neutral against 7-9% in the references, so the silhouette outline (#231d28 and similar) reads as a near-black sticker line instead of a dark material tone. The candidate has only 32 distinct colours against 66 and 185 in the references, and the large plaster wall areas are mostly flat cream with only sparse speckle. Overall it is thinner and more sticker-like than the references.
